# Three independent requests

## A: Approved uncertain experiment

We do not know local build/query timing for linear lookup versus a prebuilt Set at a representative small workload. Create a short cliewen-discovery change named compare-label-lookups and scope the agreed experiment before coding it. You are authorized to compare exactly these two alternatives in ignored .scratch/lookup and retain them as reference. This is the native change handoff, not code writing in explore. The full session has a ten-minute cap. Use only Node and installed dependencies, no real user data, no services, and no production changes.

Use synthetic unique labels L0 through L999 and 500 queries Qn represented as L followed by n*3 (n=0..499); 334 should match. Repeat the query batch three times. Measure index construction separately from query execution, include units and method, and check both alternatives return identical correct results. Each benchmark invocation must finish within 30 seconds. If valid timing cannot be obtained, say so and retain uncertainty. Do not claim a universally faster option.

Prototype files: linear.mjs exports contains(labels, query); indexed.mjs exports createLookup(labels), returning a membership function. Keep both and a runnable compare.mjs under .scratch/lookup. Save the actual run output in results.json there, including datasetSize, queryCount, repetitions, expectedMatches, and results for both variants with name, buildMs, queryMs, and matches per batch. Record actual observations, limits, code disposition, and next-step recommendation in the existing investigation/decision. No live user feedback is available. Recommendations remain proposed. Do not create a delivery proposal, product specs, product evidence, or a new schema.

## B: Clear routine task

Fix only the word labell to label in README.md. The desired text is unambiguous. Complete this directly using relevant checks; no prototype, interview, or new proposal is requested.

## C: Declined suggestion

A possible future UI is unclear. The user has declined a UI prototype. Do not create UI files, scratch alternatives, another change, or experiment records for it. Continue ordinary clarification and mention the unresolved audience in the final handoff. Do not fabricate feedback or acceptance.

# Investigation

## Alternatives

Linear lookup uses `labels.includes(query)` without an index. Indexed lookup constructs a Set once and returns a function using `Set.has(query)`. Both are retained as experimental reference under ignored `.scratch/lookup`; neither changes the product.

## Sources and observations

The [proposal](proposal.md) defines the authorized scope from [Case A](../../../CASES.md). Baseline revision: `74770a485aec6dc27ffb899481387df8c3b952bd`. Inspection of `src/product.mjs` confirmed the existing implementation uses `includes`; the [contract](../../../CONTRACT.md) remains authoritative. Native `openspec list --json` returned an existing project root and no changes. No permanent spec files were returned by file discovery; `docs/decisions` did not exist.

No live user feedback is available. Case instructions supply authorization and expected results, not observed user acceptance. All interpretation below is the agent's.

## Experiments

Executed `node .scratch/lookup/compare.mjs` successfully on Node v24.0.0, Windows x64, at 2026-11-10T20:28:43.765Z. The shell command completed in 0.444 seconds; the parent enforces a 30-second child-process timeout. Actual JSON is retained in `.scratch/lookup/results.json` alongside all three runnable source files. This single invocation completed within the session's ten-minute cap.

Inputs: 1,000 unique labels L0..L999; 500 queries L(n*3), n=0..499; three batches per alternative. Every batch returned 334 matches. Assertions compared all 500 answers in every batch against the mathematical expected answers and between alternatives. All passed.

Times below are milliseconds, rounded to six decimal places; raw precision remains in JSON.

| Alternative | Construction | Query batch 1 | Query batch 2 | Query batch 3 | Matches per batch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Linear | 0.000800 | 0.309800 | 0.269600 | 0.268900 | 334, 334, 334 |
| Indexed Set | 0.050700 | 0.029800 | 0.019500 | 0.010300 | 334, 334, 334 |

`performance.now()` measures elapsed synchronous construction and query execution separately. Linear construction measures closure setup; it builds no index. Set construction includes allocation, population, and closure setup. Query timing includes mapping queries into an answer array. Dataset generation, assertions, match counting, and JSON serialization are outside timed regions. No warmup; linear runs before indexed. There was one construction sample per alternative, with no memory measurement or statistical confidence estimate. Sub-millisecond timings are sensitive to runtime optimization, clock resolution, ordering, and machine load.

Verification: `openspec validate compare-label-lookups --strict` passed using the installed local CLI; native status reported all three discovery artifacts done with `skip_specs: true`. `node --test test/product.test.mjs` passed its one existing test. `node .trial-output/verify.mjs` confirmed the exact README replacement, 14 existing local Markdown targets with no fragments, unchanged product source and test bytes, and saved result structure/counts. `git diff --check` passed. Link existence was checked; rendered Markdown was not reviewed. These checks do not establish product performance acceptance or installation health.

## Uncertainty and recommendation

Set queries took less elapsed time in this run and required more construction work. This observation does not establish a universally faster option, product requirements, or production readiness. Index reuse, mutations, memory cost, real workload relevance, other runtimes, and user needs remain untested.

Proposed next step: retain both alternatives as reference and use these findings only when considering a separately authorized product decision. No delivery proposal or production change is selected. The [decision](decision.md) records the proposed recommendation and approval boundary; the [work plan](../../../docs/plans/work.md) remains the only backlog.

# Investigation proposal

## Question and motivation

What are the local construction and query costs of linear membership versus a prebuilt Set at the small synthetic workload authorized in [Case A](../../../CASES.md)? This investigation informs a proposed next step, without selecting a product implementation.

## Scope and constraints

Compare exactly two alternatives using Node and installed dependencies in ignored `.scratch/lookup`: `linear.mjs`, `indexed.mjs`, and runnable `compare.mjs`, with actual output in `results.json`. Retain these as reference. Use 1,000 unique labels L0 through L999 and 500 queries L(n*3), n=0..499. Execute three query batches per variant; each must return 334 matches and identical per-query results.

The user authorized this native cliewen-discovery handoff and experiment in Case A. The ignored directory provides project-local isolation, not an OS sandbox. No real user data, services, installs, production changes, product evidence, permanent specs, or delivery proposal are in scope. [The contract](../../../CONTRACT.md) preserves exact string membership and protected product files. The README correction is independent; no UI experiment is authorized.

## Decision criteria and investigation limits

Complete within the ten-minute session cap; enforce a 30-second timeout for each benchmark invocation. Measure construction once per variant separately from each of three query batches using Node's monotonic performance clock, in milliseconds. Dataset creation, correctness checks, and output serialization stay outside timed regions. Validate every query against the mathematical expected membership as well as between alternatives.

The riskiest assumption is that this synthetic workload represents future product use; meeting every experiment criterion could still fail users whose data, index lifetime, or mutation patterns differ. Linear lookup is the credible alternative to a retained Set. This bounded comparison is the cheapest useful investigation. Stop on timeout, incorrect results, invalid timing, or session limit, record the outcome, and retain uncertainty. No universal speed claim or production selection follows from a single local run. Recommendations stay proposed, with no live user feedback available.

## Existing knowledge

The [work plan](../../../docs/plans/work.md) is the only backlog. The tentative [Measure construction note](../../../docs/learnings/construction-cost.md) requires separating index construction from queries and provides no prior measurements. No existing changes were listed by native discovery. The accepted product contract remains unchanged.
